source_span: Yet again, the main driver was a big jump in energy prices, with Brent crude surging above $107/bbl... So that led to mounting speculation about faster rate hikes, while a hawkish ECB decision and a smaller-than-signaled Treasury buyback then gave the selloff even more momentum.
source_chain: Brent crude surges to $107.63 (+6.34%) on Strait of Hormuz closure fears, therefore energy-driven PPI components feeding PCE come in firm and futures lift September hike odds from 60% to 72%, therefore Treasury yields surge across the curve (2yr 4.59%, 10yr 4.96%, 30yr 5.36%), therefore the Treasury's buyback ($5.19bn, short of the announced $6bn max) fails to arrest the selloff; invalidation is today's CPI print, where a rounded 0.2% core lets the Fed hold and 0.3% forces a hike.
pulse_chain: Brent crude closes 6.34% higher at $107.63, therefore firmer PPI components feeding the Fed's preferred gauge push September hike odds from 60% to 72%, therefore 10yr/30yr/2yr yields hit multi-year highs, therefore the Treasury's $5.19bn buyback (short of its $6bn max) fails to stem the rise; invalidation is today's CPI, with JPMorgan's Feroli treating 0.2% as low enough to hold and 0.3% as high enough to hike.
why: Every step, figure, and the invalidation condition trace directly to DB's Early Morning Reid note in the same order and direction, and the DB-vs-ING debate and JPMorgan/Goldman CPI forecasts checked against their own source files (Monthly Chartbook, ING 10yr note, JPM morning briefing, GS midday color) all match without reversal or misattributed bank.
